processing_notes: Source states: 'En date du 24 juin alors que le foyer Est pouvait être considéré comme bien contrôlé et en très nette régression, son prolongement Nord restait inquiétant. processing_notes: Source states: 'The first cases were reported around 15 May, from the region of Chari-Baguirmi in which the capital is situated; within 2 weeks, more than 1 500 cases and 80 deaths had been officially reported.' - interpreted as 1500 sCh cases, 80 deaths. First two weeks of the 1991 epidemic in the Chari-Baguirmi prefecture, which then contained N'Djamena (JHU multi-unit Location, as row 421 for 1996), read as a LOWER BOUND of 1,500 suspected cases ('more than 1 500') and 80 deaths. The epidemic had not yet spread beyond Chari-Baguirmi (other prefectures by 15 June), so this is also the national count for 15-29 May 1991. First sub-national count for 1991 in the dataset; nested in the JHU WHO-annual national 1991 row (13,915/1,344). Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record 1991 vol 66 no 42 (18 October 1991) Cholera in Africa
processing_notes: Source states: 'By 15 June, the epidemic had spread to the Prefectures of Batha, Kanem, Lac, Ouaddai, Logone occidental, Mayo Kebbi and Guera, giving rise to more than 3 300 cases and 310 deaths. Two hundred and ninety cases were reported from Massakory, a town on the frontier with Cameroon.' - interpreted as 290 sCh cases. Massakory town (then Chari-Baguirmi prefecture, now Hadjer-Lamis province) cumulative from the 1991 onset (~15 May) to 15 June 1991, read as 290 suspected cases (deaths not given). WER calls Massakory 'a town on the frontier with Cameroon' - a geographic slip (Massakory is ~150 km north-east of N'Djamena); the town is unambiguous. National context: >3,300 cases/310 deaths by 15 June. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.

processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2004-06-14..2004-08-22. Source states: 'A total of 2,046 cases and 98 deaths (case fatality rate, 4.8%) have been reported from 14 June to 22 August 2004 in Western Chad, some distance from the refugee camps in the east of the country. [...] No cases have been reported from the Eastern part of Chad where the refugees from Darfur are gathering, though they are seen to be at high risk.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. WHO states explicitly that no cholera cases were reported from eastern Chad, where the Darfur refugees were gathering, during the first ten weeks of the 2004 epidemic (14 Jun-22 Aug 2004; 2,046 cases, all in western Chad: Massaguet/Hadjer-Lamis, Lac, Kanem, N'Djamena). Region: Ouaddai (then including today's Sila), mapped to post-2018 ADM1. Surveillance partial: the eastern EWARS only started in week 1 of 2005 (meta 142), but WHO/UNHCR camp health monitoring and GTFCC preparedness for the refugee areas were under way. Confidence 0.7. The later DON (2004DON145, 27 Sep) reports spread only to Mongo and Ati, 'two areas between N'Djamena and Abeche', still short of the east, but this row ends at 22 Aug as the explicit statement does. Regional cross-check: Darfur had no cholera reported in 2004 (WER 81(31) notes a 2004 preventive OCV campaign in Darfur); Nigeria 4,477 and Cameroon 2,847 cases in 2005 per WER 81(31), and Nigeria active in 2004. Agent 3 (B6-Q4).

Ouaddai' claim (meta 36) was rejected in batch 2 as a garbled 2019 count. Regional cross-check: MIXED. Cameroon (1,840, Far North and North, cross-border with Mayo-Kebbi Est) and Nigeria (2,486) were in epidemic; Niger (0) quiet; Sudan's 2019 outbreak (Blue Nile, Sennar) was far from the Chad border. source: OCHA Tchad Bulletin Humanitaire No 06 1 octobre-30 novembre 2014
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2014-07-28..2014-11-30. Source states: 'De la fin août à la fin octobre, 172 cas de choléra dont 10 décès, ont été enregistrés dans les régions du Mayo-Kebbi Ouest et du Lac. N'Djamena (2 cases in the HNO) and Mayo-Kebbi Est (Bongor department, the focus of the DG ECHO mission) are deliberately excluded. Absence is implied by concordant exhaustive breakdowns, not an explicit zero, so confidence is held at or below 0.6. The regional platform's single case in week 49 (1-7 Dec 2014) has no location and falls after this window. Regional cross-check: neighbours IN EPIDEMIC (Nigeria 35,996, Cameroon 3,355, Niger 2,059 cases in 2014). Borders Cameroon, Niger or CAR, so confidence 0.55. Agent 3 (credited to B9-Q20, OCHA bulletin 06 retrieval; meta 57).

Source states: 'The epidemic quickly spread, affecting the towns of Moundou and Bongor in the south, Bol, Massakory and Guitté near Lake Chad, and Mao in the Kanem region. The table below provides details of the situation as of 20 September: 155 4,421 Total 12 237 Guitté 2 10 Moundou 3 7 Mandelao 1 3 Mousson 17 499 Massakory 9 127 Bol 2 7 Mao 6 39 Léré 4 9 Bousso 9 87 Bongor 90 3,396 Ndjaména'. processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2004-06-14..2004-09-19. ACF 2010 Tableau 2 (meta 54), built from the WHO/SSEI weekly reports, lists exactly the same 2004 zones. The ReliefWeb copy reads '19 August', but the case sequence (2,046 to 22 Aug in DON 144) shows the data date is 19 September. The 2004 prefecture '(Mayo-Kebbi Est|Mayo-Kebbi Ouest)' appears in neither account, so absence is INFERRED (no source states 'only these regions'), with confidence held at or below 0.5. Surveillance partial (ACF: SSEI weekly district data only partially available for 2004). 1994-2010 epidemics usually reached the Fianga/Mayo-Kebbi focus, and the region borders Cameroon (8,005 cases in 2004), hence 0.45. Regional cross-check: neighbours in epidemic (Cameroon 8,005, Nigeria 3,186, Niger 2,178, CAR 320 cases in 2004, JHU). Agent 3 (credited to B6-Q4, DON 145 retrieval; re-read via ReliefWeb in B11-Q9; meta 41).

Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. WHO's official IHR list of cholera-infected areas for Chad names 12 prefectures as at 22 Aug 1996 (WER 71(34)) and the same 12 as at 19 Sep 1996 (WER 71(38)). Mayo-Kebbi Ouest) is NOT among them; neither are Moyen-Chari/Mayo-Kebbi (whichever is not this row) and Salamat (row 188). Up to 14 Jul all cases were in Chari-Baguirmi (WHO DON; row Mayo-Kebbi|1180 covers 3 Jun-14 Jul). This row extends that absence to 19 Sep 1996. It is INFERRED from non-listing: an area that had cases and was notified free before 22 Aug would also be absent from the list. Confidence 0.5. Surveillance partial (passive DSIS; weekly reporting activated during epidemics, Richard 1999). Regional cross-check: Cameroon reported 1,347 cases in July 1996 alone (WER 71(35)) and borders Mayo-Kebbi, so absence there sits beside an epidemic neighbour. Agent 3 (credited to B12-Q17, WER 71(38); concordant with B12-Q15, WER 71(34); meta 167).
